I have a complete picture. Here is my full report on the tmux URL-opening feature.

## Summary

`prefix + u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the current pane; selecting one opens it in the browser. It is powered by the third-party TPM plugin **`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`** (a fork of `wenxuangm/tmux-fzf-url`). There is **no custom script** in this repo for it — the config is a single `@plugin` line using all plugin defaults. A separate, complementary feature (`tmux-open`, copy-mode `o`) also opens URLs.

Note the capital/lowercase split: `prefix + u` (lowercase) is the URL picker; `prefix + U` (uppercase) is an unrelated "CLI tools" picker via `tv tools`.

## 1. The keybinding

The binding is **not** written explicitly in this repo's config — it is registered by the plugin itself, which defaults to `u`. This repo does not override `@fzf-url-bind`, so the effective binding is `prefix + u`.

- Plugin declaration: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`
  ```
  # URL picker: prefix + u opens fzf popup with all URLs in the pane
  set -g @plugin 'joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url'
  ```
- The actual `bind-key` is created at runtime by the plugin's loader, `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.tmux` (last line):
  ```
  key="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-bind' 'u')"
  ...
  tmux bind-key "$key" run -b "$SCRIPT_DIR/fzf-url.sh '$extra_filter' $history_limit";
  ```
  Since `@fzf-url-bind` is unset in this repo, `key` = `u`.

I confirmed there is no `bind-key u` (lowercase) and no `@fzf-url-*` override anywhere in `dot_config/tmux/`. The only `u`-family binding in `keybindings.conf.tmpl` is the uppercase `U` at line 434 (`tv tools`, a different feature).

## 2. Mechanism & installation

- **Type:** third-party tmux plugin, `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (GitHub repo `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`; original author Wenxuan `wenxuangm`, per the header in `fzf-url.tmux`).
- **Install path:** TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager).
  - TPM itself is cloned by chezmoi external: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl:129` → clones `https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm.git` into `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`.
  - TPM is run at the end of the tmux config: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf:26` → `run 'PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'` (macOS prepends GNU coreutils for plugins expecting GNU utils).
  - Plugins are populated on first setup by Ansible: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4178-4200` ("Install tmux plugins via TPM", runs `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/install_plugins`, guarded by a `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed` sentinel). Manual fallback is `prefix + I` inside tmux.
  - Installed on this host at `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/` (cloned 21 Apr).

## 3. How URLs are extracted and opened (the picker)

The worker script is `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh`. Because this repo sets no options, it runs with defaults: `history_limit='screen'` and no extra filter.

Flow:
1. **Capture pane content** — default `limit=screen` → `content="$(tmux capture-pane -J -p)"` (visible screen only; a numeric `@fzf-url-history-limit` would instead capture `-S -<N>` lines of scrollback).
2. **Extract candidates** via multiple `grep -oE` passes over the captured text:
   - `urls`: `(https?|ftp|file):/?//...`
   - `wwws`: bare `www.` hosts, prefixed with `http://`
   - `ips`: `d.d.d.d(:port)(/path)`, prefixed with `http://`
   - `gits`: `git@...` SSH remotes rewritten to `https://`
   - `gh`: quoted `owner/repo` strings rewritten to `https://github.com/...`
   - `npm`: `import "pkg"` statements rewritten to `https://npmjs.com/package/...`
   - `extras`: only if `@fzf-url-extra-filter` is set (it is not here)
3. **Dedupe & number**: `printf ... | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | nl -w3 -s '  '`. If empty → `tmux display 'tmux-fzf-url: no URLs found'` and exit.
4. **Pick**: `fzf_filter` runs `fzf-tmux -d 35% -m -0 --no-preview --no-border` (default `@fzf-url-fzf-options`). `-m` = multi-select, `-0` = exit if no matches.
5. **Open**: the awk-extracted URL(s) are passed to `open_url`, with a log at `/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-fzf-url.log`.

The exact opener:
```
open_url() {
    if hash xdg-open &>/dev/null; then
        nohup xdg-open "$@"
    elif hash open &>/dev/null; then
        nohup open "$@"
    elif [[ -n $BROWSER ]]; then
        nohup "$BROWSER" "$@"
    fi
}
```

## 4. Related scripts

No repo-managed script implements this — the extraction/opening lives entirely in the vendored plugin (`~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh` and `fzf-url.tmux`), installed via TPM as above. The many scripts under `dot_config/tmux/` (menus, sesh pickers, etc.) are unrelated.

## 5. Cross-platform open handling

Handled inside the plugin's `open_url` (above): it prefers **`xdg-open`** (Linux) if present, else **`open`** (macOS), else falls back to **`$BROWSER`**. On macOS `xdg-open` is normally absent, so `open` is used. Note the order means that if `xdg-open` exists (e.g. installed on macOS via coreutils/ports), it would win over `open`. Each launch is wrapped in `nohup` so it detaches from tmux.

## Bonus: the complementary copy-mode opener (tmux-open)

Also relevant to "opening URLs from tmux" — `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:39-41`:
```
# Open highlighted selection in copy-mode: o = open, C-o = open in $EDITOR, S = search
set -g @plugin 'tmux-plugins/tmux-open'
set -g @open-S 'https://www.google.com/search?q='
```
In copy mode: `o` opens the highlighted selection (URL/file) in the default app, `C-o` opens it in `$EDITOR`, and `S` searches the selection on Google. Documented at `docs/tools/tmux/keybindings.md:226-228`.

# herdr — full findings

## 1. What herdr is + how it's installed

**herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer with built-in AI coding-agent awareness** (tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). Same niche as tmux/zellij, but mouse-first and agent-native. In this repo it's a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** (you run one or the other, never nested by default).

- **Upstream repo:** `https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr` (confirmed by the GitHub API URL in the ansible install task, `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4673`: `https://api.github.com/repos/ogulcancelik/herdr/releases/latest`).
- **Docs site:** `https://herdr.dev/docs/` — config schema at `https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/`.
- **Plugin ecosystem:** `cloudmanic/herdr-plus` (`https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus`) adds "Projects" + "Quick Actions".
- **Hierarchy:** Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane (one level deeper than tmux).

**Install** (`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`):
- macOS: Homebrew formula `herdr` (homebrew-core), listed in the brew block at line 89.
- Linux/Debian: GitHub release single static binary `herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}` → `~/.local/bin/herdr` (install block starts at line 4628; the `--- herdr ---` comment). No tarball/unarchive.
- herdr-plus plugin: `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes` (block at line 4713).

## 2. Config file — exact source paths

The live target is `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, produced by a chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (tomlkit). Two source files:

| Role | Source path |
|---|---|
| Overlay script (the `modify_`) | `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` |
| Managed body (the actual config content) | `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` |

**Helper scripts** in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/`:
- `executable_pane-copy.sh` → `~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` (reads pane content/coords, pipes to clipboard)
- `executable_review-mark.sh` → review-pending ⭐ flag toggler
- `executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh` → new tab at workspace root

**herdr-plus Quick Actions** (one TOML per action) in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` — includes URL-opening starters: `github.toml`, `google.toml`, `google-search.toml`, `open-repo.toml`, `open-working-dir.toml`, plus four `copy-pane-*.toml`.

**Television channels** (herdr-aware pickers) in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/`: `herdr-sesh.toml`, `herdr-agent-panes.toml`, `herdr-review.toml`.

## 3. Config schema / tables

The managed body (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`) defines these tables. The overlay **enforces** `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, `[keys]` on every apply and **preserves** everything herdr writes back at runtime (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`).

- `[theme]` — `name`, `auto_switch`, `light_name`, `dark_name`
- `[ui]` — `mouse_capture`, `pane_borders`, `pane_gaps`, `confirm_close`, `show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders`
- `[terminal]` — `shell_mode`, `new_cwd`
- `[keys]` — **rebinds of built-in actions** + repeated **`[[keys.command]]`** array-of-tables for custom bindings
- `[session]` — `resume_agents_on_restore` (runtime-owned)
- `[remote]` — `manage_ssh_config` (runtime-owned)

Prefix is `ctrl+b` (herdr default = tmux default). **Yes, herdr has full keybinding support**, two flavors: rebinding fixed built-in actions, and defining custom command bindings that run arbitrary shell (`type = "pane"`, plus `plugin_action`). It has a first-class notion of **panes and captured pane output** (`herdr pane read`), and opening things (via custom commands → `x open`).

## 4. herdr keybinding format — this is what matters for the URL picker

### Built-in action rebinds (fixed action set, value is a key or array of keys)
```toml
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"   # "N..M" indexed-range form
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
```

### Custom command panes — `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables (the URL-picker vehicle)
This is herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. `type = "pane"` opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits. The command runs from the focused pane's cwd and receives env vars `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`.

Exact shape (verbatim examples from the current config):
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+U"
type = "pane"
command = "tv tools"
description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+m"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh toggle \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"
```

`plugin_action` type (herdr-plus):
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+y"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"
```

### Quick Action TOML format (herdr-plus, one file per action)
Types: `command`, `form`, `select`. Templating: `{{.Value}}`, `{{.WorkDir}}`, filters like `{{.Value | urlquery}}`.
```toml
name = "Search Google"
type = "form"
command = "x open 'https://www.google.com/search?q={{.Value | urlquery}}'"
[form]
prompt = "Search Google for"
placeholder = "e.g. herdr terminal multiplexer"
```

### Key-syntax gotchas (documented in the config comments)
- Uppercase letter = `prefix+shift+<letter>`. herdr reserves `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane), `shift+g`, `shift+t`.
- `prefix+shift+<digit>` does NOT work under the Kitty keyboard protocol (shift+1 emits `!`). Use `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` for indexed jumps.
- Validate any edit with `herdr server reload-config` — an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means no keybind collisions.

## 5. modify_ overlay mechanism (`docs/tools/herdr.md` "Config management" + CLAUDE.md line 183)

`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` is a POSIX-sh script. chezmoi pipes the live target into stdin; the script prints the new file to stdout. Merge model:
- Base = the managed template `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` (pulled in via `{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}` written to a temp file through a heredoc redirect — done that way because the config contains a lone backtick in `key = "prefix+\`"` that breaks `$(...)` capture).
- For every top-level key in the live file NOT in `{theme, ui, terminal, keys}`, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding/session/remote/update/experimental writeback).
- Managed tables win wholesale (in-app theme/label overrides are re-asserted).
- Runs in Python via `uv run --no-project --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11'` (tomlkit round-trips comments + the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables). Degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw template. Read side uses stdlib `tomllib`/`tomli`.
- **To manage a new key you edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`** (NOT the modify_ script). CLAUDE.md warns: never `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target.

Note: `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md` does not exist; the relevant docs are `docs/tools/herdr.md` and `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` (CLAUDE.md line 183 summarizes the `modify_` prefix behavior).

## 6. Directly relevant to "quickly open URLs like tmux's picker"

### The tmux model the user is copying
`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`: `prefix + u` → plugin `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (TPM-installed) opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the pane; selecting one opens it. Also `tmux-plugins/tmux-open` (`o` in copy-mode opens highlighted URL). Documented in `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md:29`.

### There is currently NO herdr URL picker
Grepping the herdr config, helpers, and tv channels found zero URL-picker binding. `prefix+u` (lowercase) is **free** in herdr — the config only binds `prefix+U` (shift+u) to `tv tools` (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml:130-134`). So lowercase `prefix+u` is available and matches tmux muscle memory.

### The building blocks to implement it (all already present in the repo)
1. **Extract pane text** (the URL source): `herdr pane read <pane> --source visible|recent --format text` — used in `dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:132`. `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` gives the focused pane inside a `[[keys.command]]`; fall back to `herdr pane current | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id'` (pattern at pane-copy.sh:76-78).
2. **Pick a URL**: pipe extracted URLs through `fzf` (available) or a `tv` channel — same command-pane popup mechanism already used for `tv tools`/`lazygit`.
3. **Open cross-platform**: `x open <url>` — the repo's own opener (wslview / open / xdg-open), already used by every URL Quick Action (`github.toml`, `google.toml`, etc.).

### The natural implementation shape (a `[[keys.command]]` in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`)
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
```
where a new `dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh` would `herdr pane read` → grep URLs → `fzf` → `x open`. This mirrors the existing `pane-copy.sh` helper exactly (same `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` handling, same `herdr pane read` call, same `x` absolute-path fallback for command panes that run via `sh -c` without the interactive PATH). Alternatively it can be added purely as a herdr-plus Quick Action TOML, but the keybinding-pane route matches the tmux `prefix+u` UX one-to-one.

This exact task ("port tmux `prefix + u` URL opening to herdr") was already started in today's session `.specstory/history/2026-07-17_07-30-59Z-tmux-prefix-u-url.md` — worth reading for any prior decisions, though no URL picker has been committed to the config yet.
```

/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md:175:**Clean quit**: "Kill session & exit", "Kill all sessions (clean)", `prefix + M-Q`, and `tmux-kill-clean` clear tmux-resurrect's `last` symlink so tmux-continuum does NOT auto-restore the just-closed sessions on the next tmux start. `tmux-forget-last` / "Forget auto-restore" clears only that symlink and leaves the server running. Other kill paths (`kill-pane`, `kill-window`, plain `kill-session` when other sessions remain) do NOT touch it — the server stays alive so no restore is triggered anyway. Crash recovery is unaffected: historical snapshots stay, `prefix + Ctrl-r` can still restore manually.

```text
1	#!/bin/sh
2	# chezmoi modify_ script: overlay a managed herdr config onto ~/.config/herdr/config.toml.
3	#
4	# Why: herdr can rewrite this file at runtime (onboarding flag, in-app settings
5	# popups, [session]/[remote]/[update] state), so tracking it as a plain managed
6	# file would clobber that writeback and re-trigger onboarding. It was previously
7	# `create_` (seed-once), but that meant repo edits never reached an
8	# already-seeded host without a manual refresh. This modify_ overlay enforces
9	# our managed tables ([theme], [ui], [terminal], [keys]) on every `chezmoi
10	# apply` while preserving every other top-level key herdr writes back.
11	#
12	# How: chezmoi pipes the current target file into stdin; this script prints the
13	# new contents on stdout.
14	#
15	# Merge model — template-as-base, pull-through unmanaged keys:
16	#   - Base = the managed template (.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml), which
17	#     carries the comments + the tmux-parity rationale.
18	#   - For every TOP-LEVEL key in the live file NOT in {theme, ui, terminal,
19	#     keys}, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding, [session], [remote],
20	#     [update], [experimental], and any future herdr writeback).
21	#   - Managed tables are enforced wholesale (template wins) — this is a managed
22	#     dotfile; in-app theme/label overrides are intentionally re-asserted.
23	#
24	# Why tomlkit (not codex's inline emitter): herdr's config has an
25	# array-of-tables ([[keys.command]]) and comments we want to keep; stdlib
26	# tomllib is read-only and the codex modify_ emitter can't emit AoT. tomlkit
27	# round-trips both.
28	#
29	# Note: the template is written to a temp file via a heredoc *redirect* (not
30	# captured with $(...)), because the config body contains a lone backtick
31	# (`key = "prefix+\`"`) that bash mis-parses as command substitution when a
32	# quoted heredoc is nested inside $(...). Passing the path to Python sidesteps it.
33	#
34	# To manage an additional key: edit .chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml.
35	# Python runtime: prefer `uv` (guarantees Python >=3.11 → stdlib tomllib), fall
36	# back to system python3, then to printing the raw template unmodified (a
37	# fresh-bootstrap host with neither uv nor python3 still gets a full config —
38	# note we print the TEMPLATE, not stdin, because on a fresh host stdin is empty).
39	set -eu
40	
41	tmpl_file=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/herdr-config.XXXXXX")
42	trap 'rm -f "$tmpl_file"' EXIT INT TERM
43	
44	cat <<'TOML' > "$tmpl_file"
45	{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}
46	TOML
47	
48	live=$(cat)
49	
50	if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
51	  set -- uv run --no-project --quiet --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11' python -
52	elif command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
53	  set -- python3 -
54	else
55	  echo "modify_config.toml: neither uv nor python3 found; emitting managed template" >&2
56	  cat "$tmpl_file"
57	  exit 0
58	fi
59	
60	HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE="$tmpl_file" HERDR_LIVE="$live" "$@" <<'PYEOF'
61	import os
62	import sys
63	
64	tmpl_path = os.environ["HERDR_TEMPLATE_FILE"]
65	with open(tmpl_path, "r") as fh:
66	    template_text = fh.read()
67	
68	
69	def emit_template():
70	    sys.stdout.write(template_text)
71	
72	
73	# Read side: stdlib tomllib (uv guarantees >=3.11); tomli backport otherwise.
74	try:
75	    import tomllib  # Python 3.11+
76	except ModuleNotFoundError:
77	    try:
78	        import tomli as tomllib
79	    except ModuleNotFoundError:
80	        # No TOML reader → can't safely merge; ship the managed template as-is
81	        # (loses runtime-key preservation, but keeps the host configured).
82	        emit_template()
83	        sys.exit(0)
84	
85	# Write side: tomlkit preserves comments + array-of-tables. uv installs it via
86	# --with tomlkit; a bare system python3 may lack it → fall back to raw template.
87	try:
88	    import tomlkit
89	except ModuleNotFoundError:
90	    print(
91	        "modify_config.toml: tomlkit unavailable; emitting managed template "
92	        "(runtime keys not preserved this run)",
93	        file=sys.stderr,
94	    )
95	    emit_template()
96	    sys.exit(0)
97	
98	MANAGED = {"theme", "ui", "terminal", "keys"}
99	
100	live_text = os.environ.get("HERDR_LIVE", "").strip()
101	doc = tomlkit.parse(template_text)  # base, with comments intact
102	live = tomllib.loads(live_text) if live_text else {}
103	
104	# Pull through every top-level key herdr owns at runtime that we don't manage.
105	for key, value in live.items():
106	    if key in MANAGED or key in doc:
107	        continue
108	    doc[key] = value
109	
110	sys.stdout.write(tomlkit.dumps(doc))
111	PYEOF
112

=== /Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash

get_fzf_options() {
	local fzf_options
	local fzf_default_options='-d 35% -m -0 --no-preview --no-border'
	fzf_options="$(tmux show -gqv '@fzf-url-fzf-options')"
	[ -n "$fzf_options" ] && echo "$fzf_options" || echo "$fzf_default_options"
}

fzf_filter() {
	eval "fzf-tmux $(get_fzf_options)"
}

open_url() {
	if hash xdg-open &>/dev/null; then
		nohup xdg-open "$@"
	elif hash open &>/dev/null; then
		nohup open "$@"
	elif [[ -n $BROWSER ]]; then
		nohup "$BROWSER" "$@"
	fi
}

limit='screen'
[[ $# -ge 2 ]] && limit=$2

if [[ $limit == 'screen' ]]; then
	content="$(tmux capture-pane -J -p)"
else
	content="$(tmux capture-pane -J -p -S -"$limit")"
fi

urls=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE '(https?|ftp|file):/?//[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%?=~_|!:,.;]*[-A-Za-z0-9+&@#/%=~_|]')
wwws=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE '(http?s://)?www\.[a-zA-Z](-?[a-zA-Z0-9])+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,}(/\S+)*' | grep -vE '^https?://' | sed 's/^\(.*\)$/http:\/\/\1/')
ips=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE '[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}(:[0-9]{1,5})?(/\S+)*' | sed 's/^\(.*\)$/http:\/\/\1/')
gits=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE '(ssh://)?git@\S*' | sed 's/:/\//g' | sed 's/^\(ssh\/\/\/\)\{0,1\}git@\(.*\)$/https:\/\/\2/')
gh=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE "['\"]([A-Za-z0-9-]*/[.A-Za-z0-9-]*)['\"]" | sed "s/['\"]//g" | sed 's#.#https://github.com/&#')
npm=$(echo "$content" | grep -oE "import\s+[^\"';]*[\"']([^.][^\"';]*)[\"']" | sed "s/[^'\"]*['\"]\([^'\"]*\)['\"];*/\1/" | sed 's@.@https:\/\/npmjs.com\/package\/&@')

if [[ $# -ge 1 && "$1" != '' ]]; then
	extras=$(echo "$content" | eval "$1")
fi

items=$(
	printf '%s\n' "${urls[@]}" "${wwws[@]}" "${gh[@]}" "${npm[@]}" "${ips[@]}" "${gits[@]}" "${extras[@]}" |
		grep -v '^$' |
		sort -u |
		nl -w3 -s '  '
)
[ -z "$items" ] && tmux display 'tmux-fzf-url: no URLs found' && exit

fzf_filter <<<"$items" | awk '{print $2}' |
	while read -r chosen; do
		open_url "$chosen" &>"/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-fzf-url.log"
	done
=== /Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.tmux ===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
#===============================================================================
#   Author: Wenxuan
#    Email: wenxuangm@gmail.com
#  Created: 2018-04-06 09:30
#===============================================================================
SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)

# $1: option
# $2: default value
tmux_get() {
    local value
    value="$(tmux show -gqv "$1")"
    [ -n "$value" ] && echo "$value" || echo "$2"
}

key="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-bind' 'u')"
history_limit="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-history-limit' 'screen')"
extra_filter="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-extra-filter' '')"
echo "$extra_filter" > /tmp/filter

tmux bind-key "$key" run -b "$SCRIPT_DIR/fzf-url.sh '$extra_filter' $history_limit";
```

```text
1	# Herdr — Rust terminal multiplexer + AI-agent orchestrator (trial)
2	
3	[ogulcancelik/herdr](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr) is a Rust terminal multiplexer with **built-in coding-agent awareness** (it tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). It sits in the same niche as tmux/zellij but is mouse-first and agent-native. Docs: <https://herdr.dev/docs/>.
4	
5	This repo ships herdr as a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** — you run `herdr` *or* `tmux`, never nested. Nothing about the existing tmux / `sesh` / `tmuxp` / workmux setup changes; herdr is purely additive so you can evaluate it without losing your daily driver.
6	
7	- **Install**:
8	  - macOS — Homebrew (`herdr` is in homebrew-core; managed by the `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` macOS list)
9	  - Linux — GitHub release **single static binary** (`herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}`) into `~/.local/bin/herdr` (managed by the `# --- herdr ... ---` block in the same role). No tarball, so no unarchive step.
10	- **Verify**: `herdr --version` · validate config with `herdr server reload-config`
11	- **Upgrade**: brew on macOS; `herdr update` for the self-managed Linux binary
12	- **Config**: `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` — chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` + managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`). The overlay enforces our managed tables on every `chezmoi apply` while preserving whatever herdr writes back at runtime (see [Config management](#config-management-why-modify_)).
13	
14	> **Not gated by `enableVimMode`.** That flag governs shell + tmux modal editing; herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style natively regardless (`h/j/k/l`, `w/b/e`, `{`/`}`, `v`/Space to select, `y`/Enter to copy, `q`/Esc to leave), so there is nothing to gate.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Model differences vs tmux
19	
20	herdr's hierarchy is **Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane** — one level deeper than tmux (Session → Window → Pane). A "Workspace" is a project-level container; a "Tab" groups panes. The CLI (`herdr session|workspace|tab|pane|agent …`, most with `--json`) is the scripting surface that replaces `tmux switch-client` / `list-sessions` etc.
21	
22	The important twist vs tmux: a single herdr **server hosts multiple named sessions**, each its own persistent tree with its own socket. That top **Session** level is closer to "multiple tmux servers / sockets" than to a tmux session — the tmux thing you'd call a session (`vibe/<repo>`) maps to a herdr **Workspace**, not a herdr Session.
23	
24	### Named sessions
25	
26	- `herdr` — launch or attach the **default** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`).
27	- `herdr --session NAME` — launch/attach a **named** session (socket `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<NAME>/herdr.sock`).
28	- `herdr session list [--json]` — all sessions with `running` + `socket_path`. **The `--json` `socket_path` is authoritative** — the plain-text table prints `herdr.socket`, but the real socket is `herdr.sock`.
29	- `herdr session attach NAME` · `herdr session stop NAME` · `herdr session delete NAME` (`default` is a valid `NAME` for stop).
30	
31	**Targeting a session from the CLI subcommands**: there is **no `--session`/`--socket` flag** on `workspace`/`tab`/`pane`/`agent`. The only lever is the **`HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`** env var — set it to a session's `socket_path` and every subcommand routes there. Inside a herdr pane it is already exported to the current session's socket, so scripts run *inside* herdr target the current session for free. This is exactly how `hvibe --session NAME` works (see below).
32	
33	## cwd & workspace-naming model
34	
35	herdr tracks cwd differently from tmux, which trips up two common expectations (all verified via `herdr pane list`):
36	
37	- **Every pane has two cwds.** `cwd` = the shell's *startup* directory (fixed at spawn); `foreground_cwd` = the *live* cwd, tracked via **OSC 7** shell integration. A `cd` in the shell updates `foreground_cwd`; the startup `cwd` never changes.
38	- **`cd` inside a child process / subshell doesn't propagate.** Because tracking is OSC 7-based, a `cd` in a subshell that doesn't re-emit OSC 7 — e.g. `chezmoi cd`, which spawns a *new* shell in the source dir — is invisible to herdr. `foreground_cwd` stays put, so the space's git-repo detection and the `prefix+G` lazygit location don't follow the subshell. This is inherent to OSC 7, **not** a herdr bug — expected behavior.
39	- **New tabs follow the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x).** With `new_cwd = "follow"` (below), a *new tab* inherits the focused pane's live cwd — same as a *split*. herdr [issue #912](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/issues/912) changed `follow` so tabs behave like splits; the older "new tab opens at the workspace root (often `$HOME`)" was treated as a bug and removed. There is **no `new_cwd` value** (and no workspace-level cwd — `herdr workspace get` exposes none) that opens a new tab at the workspace root; for that use **`prefix+C`** (below).
40	- **The workspace ("space") label auto-follows the root/primary pane's live cwd basename** (e.g. → `chezmoi`, `trading-journal`). `cd` in **tab 1** renames the space; `cd` in other tabs does not. No config knob controls this.
41	
42	**`new_cwd` values** (`[terminal]`) — the CWD policy for new panes/tabs/workspaces when no explicit `--cwd` is given:
43	
44	| value | meaning |
45	|---|---|
46	| `follow` (default) | inherit the **source** pane — for both a split *and* a new tab, the focused pane's live cwd (herdr ≥0.7.x) |
47	| `home` | `$HOME` |
48	| `current` | herdr's **own process** directory (NOT the focused pane) |
49	| `"~/path"` | a fixed path |
50	
51	**No `new_cwd` value opens a new tab at the workspace ("space") root** — `follow` now tracks the focused pane, and herdr exposes no workspace-level cwd field. This repo ships that behavior as a keybind: **`prefix+C`** → `~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh` (`dot_config/herdr/executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh`), which derives the space root — the lowest-numbered tab's pane live cwd, i.e. what herdr uses for the space label — and runs `herdr tab create --workspace <wid> --cwd <root> --focus`. Native `prefix+c` **and the mouse "+" button** keep the follow-focused-pane behavior; a keybind cannot intercept the mouse button.
52	
53	```toml
54	[[keys.command]]
55	key = "prefix+C"
56	type = "pane"
57	command = "~/.config/herdr/new-tab-at-space-root.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
58	description = "new tab at the workspace (space) root dir"
59	```
60	
61	## Feasibility matrix (current tmux experience → herdr)
62	
63	| Current capability | herdr story | How it's handled here |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| Catppuccin theme + light/dark | **Native** `[theme]` + `auto_switch` | Configured in `config.toml` |
66	| Splits / zoom / new tab+workspace / pane nav | **Native** `[keys]` actions | Rebound to tmux muscle memory |
67	| Session persistence (resurrect/continuum) | **Native** detach/reattach | Skipped — native |
68	| Mouse / right-click menus | **Native** mouse-first | Skipped — native |
69	| Agent status 🤖/💬/✅ (workmux, 6 files) | **Native** agent-state rollups in sidebar | Skipped — native (workmux untouched for tmux) |
70	| `sesh` fuzzy switch + `tmuxp` layouts | **Plugin** [herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) Projects + Quick Actions | Plugin + Projects templates |
71	| `tv` channel popups (`prefix+T/U/a`) | **Custom command panes** (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) | Key bindings + 2 herdr-aware channels |
72	| lazygit / scratch popups | **Custom command panes** | Key bindings |
73	| Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane nav | **No herdr-aware smart-splits** | **Gap** — workaround below |
74	| OSC133 copy-mode (`cpout`/`cpblock`) | tmux-specific | **Gap** — `cpcmd` (zsh history) still works |
75	| Per-window status glyphs + bookmarks ⭐📌 | Partial — `report-metadata --custom-status` (per-pane, orthogonal to agent state) | **Review-pending flag** (`hmark`/`prefix+m` + `tv herdr-review` inbox); decorative status-bar glyphs still a gap (no format-string interpolation) |
76	| AI session-summary / agent-wakeup capture | re-portable against `herdr pane read` / `pane list --json` | **Deferred** — out of trial scope |
77	
78	## Keybindings
79	
80	Prefix is `ctrl+b` (same as tmux). Built-in actions can only be *rebound* (herdr's action set is fixed); everything else is a `[[keys.command]]` custom command. Custom commands receive `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD` and run from the focused pane's cwd.
81	
82	> **Two families of herdr env vars.** The `HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_*` vars above are injected **only** into `[[keys.command]]` invocations. Every shell *running inside a herdr pane* also gets an **ambient** set: `HERDR_ENV=1`, `HERDR_PANE_ID`, `HERDR_TAB_ID`, `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID`, and `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` (the current session's socket). Scripts use `HERDR_ENV` as the "am I inside herdr?" test and inherit `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` to target the current session — that's what `hvibe`/`hcode` rely on.
83	
84	| Key | Action | Type |
85	|---|---|---|
86	| `prefix + c` / `prefix + 1..9` | new tab / switch tab | built-in default |
87	| `prefix + C` | new tab at the workspace (**space**) root dir — `prefix+c` + mouse "+" stay follow-focused-pane | command pane |
88	| `prefix + h/j/k/l` | focus pane | built-in default |
89	| `prefix + \|` / `prefix + %` · `prefix + minus` / `prefix + "` | split side-by-side / stacked (tmux muscle memory — both the intuitive key and the tmux default) | rebound (arrays) |
90	| `prefix + z` / `prefix + x` | zoom / close pane | built-in default |
91	| `prefix + w` / `prefix + g` | workspace navigator (navigate-mode: **`j`/`k`** *or* arrows to move, Enter to pick) / session navigator | built-in; `navigate_workspace_*` rebound to `j`/`k` + arrows |
92	| `prefix + ctrl + 1..9` | jump directly to **workspace** N (`switch_workspace`) | rebound (indexed) |
93	| `prefix + alt + 1..9` | jump directly to **agent** N's pane (`focus_agent`) | rebound (indexed) |
94	
95	> **Why ctrl/alt, not shift, for the indexed jumps**: under the Kitty keyboard protocol (which herdr uses) `shift+1` still carries the printable `!`, so herdr matches the symbol rather than `shift+1` — `prefix+shift+1..9` silently does nothing. `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` have no printable form and disambiguate cleanly.
96	| `prefix + [` | vi copy mode (`hjkl`, `w/b/e`, `{/}`, `v`, `y`) | built-in default |
97	| `prefix + q` | detach | built-in default |
98	| `prefix + ?` | keybinds help overlay — lists every active binding with labels (herdr's native which-key; manually invoked, not an auto-timeout hint) | built-in default |
99	| `prefix + ,` | rename tab | rebound (tmux muscle memory) |
100	| `prefix + shift + r` | reload config (`prefix + r` stays resize mode) | rebound |
101	| `prefix + shift + b` | new git worktree (moved off `prefix + shift + g`) | rebound |
102	| `prefix + G` | lazygit | command pane |
103	| `prefix + M` | btop system monitor | command pane |
104	| `prefix + N` | nvtop GPU monitor | command pane |
105	| `prefix + U` | `tv tools` (CLI launcher) | command pane |
106	| `prefix + T` | `tv herdr-sesh` (workspace/dir switcher) | command pane |
107	| `prefix + a` | `tv herdr-agent-panes` (live agent panes) | command pane |
108	| `prefix + f` | `tv fleet-hosts` (SSH picker) | command pane |
109	| `prefix + m` | toggle **review-pending** flag (⭐) on the current pane | command pane |
110	| `prefix + i` | `tv herdr-review` — review-pending **inbox** (flagged panes) | command pane |
111	| `prefix + P` | copy focused pane's **process info** to the clipboard | command pane |
112	| `prefix + D` | copy focused pane's **coordinate** (session>space>tab>pane) | command pane |
113	| `prefix + V` | copy focused pane's **content** (visible screen) | command pane |
114	| `prefix + S` | copy focused pane's **content** (full scrollback) | command pane |
115	| `` prefix + ` `` | scratch shell | command pane |
116	| `prefix + O` | herdr-plus **Projects** (layout launcher) | plugin action |
117	| `prefix + y` | herdr-plus **Quick Actions** | plugin action |
118	
119	> Uppercase letters resolve to `prefix+shift+<letter>`, which herdr reserves for built-ins (`shift+g` worktree, `shift+t` rename-tab, `shift+h/j/k/l` swap-pane). `prefix+G`/`prefix+T` are freed by the rebinds above; `herdr server reload-config` reports any remaining collisions in its `diagnostics`.
120	
121	## Session helpers: `hvibe` / `hcode` / `hhere` / `hroot` (herdr analogs of `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot`)
122	
123	Four shell functions in [`dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`](../shells/aliases.md#session-management) are the herdr counterparts of the tmux `svibe` / `scode` / `shere` / `sroot` helpers. The two **heavyweight** ones (`hvibe` / `hcode`) spin up a whole coding workspace in one motion; the two **lightweight** ones (`hhere` / `hroot`) just open a plain workspace at a directory and attach — no git repo, no agent layout. They shell out to the native `herdr workspace|tab|pane` CLI and **reuse the pure logic verbatim** (specstory wrapping, `--on-exit shell|kill|restart`, git-root resolution, agent-CLI detection) from `22_sesh.sh`; only the layout calls differ. Need the `herdr` server running + `jq`.
124	
125	| Command | Builds workspace | Layout |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| `hvibe [N] [CLI]` / `hvibe --agents claude,codex,opencode` | `vibe/<repo>` | tab `agents` (N even-width agent panes) + tab `git` (lazygit) + tab `edit` (nvim) |
128	| `hvibe --tab-per-agent …` | `vibe/<repo>` | one tab **per agent** + `git` + `edit` tabs |
129	| `hcode [CLI]` | `coding-agent/<repo>` | tab `editor` (nvim 75% \| agent 25%) + tab `monitor` (btop) |
130	| `hhere [CMD...]` | `<basename $PWD>` | single tab, plain shell at `$PWD` (or `-p DIR`); optional `CMD` in the root pane |
131	| `hroot [CMD...]` | `<basename git-root>` | same as `hhere` but at the current git root (falls back to `$PWD`) |
132	
133	- **The plain-open pair (`hhere` / `hroot`)** fills the gap where every other herdr entry point forces a git repo + a full agent layout. With tmux, `tmux new-session` lands you in `$PWD` directly; herdr adds a Workspace layer, so without these you'd launch herdr, create a space (which opens at `$HOME` per `new_cwd`), then `cd` by hand. `hhere` does the one-shot: `herdr workspace create --cwd "$PWD"` → focus → attach if outside. No git requirement; the optional command runs **raw** (no specstory/on-exit wrapping — that stays with `hcode`/`hvibe`). `hhere -h` / `hroot -h` for flags. **Label caveat**: herdr auto-relabels a workspace to its root pane's *live* cwd basename after a `cd` in tab 1 (see the **cwd & workspace-naming model** section above), so the idempotent-focus is best-effort — a drifted label makes a re-run open a fresh workspace.
134	- **Idempotent per repo**: re-running focuses the existing `vibe/<repo>` / `coding-agent/<repo>` workspace instead of duplicating (matches svibe's "attach if exists").
135	- **Attach-aware (like svibe's `$TMUX` branch)**: run from **inside** herdr → the workspace/tab focus calls switch the live client (no new client). Run from a **plain terminal outside** herdr → the helper brings up a client attached to the session so the new workspace is actually visible (herdr's `workspace focus` only moves an *already-attached* client, so without this the pack was built invisibly). `--no-attach` builds detached either way. Detection is the ambient `HERDR_ENV`.
136	- **`--session NAME`** targets a specific running herdr session (see [Named sessions](#named-sessions)). Default: the **current** session when inside herdr (via inherited `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`), else the **default** session. The override is scoped with `local -x HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` so it never leaks into your shell. A `--session` that isn't running errors with a `herdr --session NAME` hint (start it first — hvibe won't spawn a server).
137	- **Agent visibility**: herdr tracks agent state **per pane**, so in the default splits layout every agent still surfaces individually in herdr's agent tracking (verified: two agents in one tab appear as two separate entries in `herdr agent list`). The compact left sidebar rolls a *tab's* status into one dot — use `--tab-per-agent` if you want each agent to own a tab-level status dot.
138	- **Even columns**: herdr has no `select-layout even-horizontal`, so `hvibe` sets each split's `--ratio` explicitly (`1/(N-m+1)`) to keep the agent panes even; `hcode` uses `--ratio 0.75` to give nvim 75%.
139	- Same flags as svibe/scode: `--on-exit`, `--no-specstory`, `--no-attach`, `-p/--path`, plus `--session NAME`; `hvibe` also takes `--min-width` / `--tab-per-agent` and honors `$HVIBE_MIN_WIDTH` / `$HVIBE_LAUNCH_STAGGER`. Full flag help: `hvibe -h` / `hcode -h`.
140	
141	The tmux `svibe` / `scode` remain the tmux-side equivalents (see [sesh](sesh.md)); the two families coexist — `hvibe`/`hcode` only touch herdr, `svibe`/`scode` only touch tmux.
142	
143	## herdr-plus plugin (sesh + tmuxp + menu analog)
144	
145	[herdr-plus](https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus) adds **Projects** (declarative multi-tab/multi-pane workspace templates with a fuzzy picker — the `tmuxp`/`tmuxinator` analog) and **Quick Actions** (a fuzzy command launcher — the popup-menu analog).
146	
147	**Install is automated** by the `devtools` ansible role (the `# --- herdr-plus plugin ---` block) — idempotent, runs on every `chezmoi apply`, skipped once installed. It shells out to:
148	
149	```bash
150	herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus   # manual fallback / what the role runs
151	```
152	
153	`herdr plugin install` **downloads a prebuilt release binary when no Go toolchain is present**, so it works with or without Go. The one trap: if a *stale* Go is on `PATH` (e.g. an old `/usr/local/go` shadowing a newer one) herdr tries to build from source and fails (`invalid go version … must match format 1.23`) instead of falling back. The ansible task sidesteps this by prepending mise's Go (`mise which go` → its bin dir) when available; to fix it by hand, put a modern Go first: `PATH="$(dirname "$(mise which go)"):$PATH" herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus`. (Go is mise-managed now, gated on `installExtraRuntimes`.)
154	
155	Project templates are chezmoi-managed under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/projects/` → the same path under `~/.config/`. The shipped `chezmoi.toml` mirrors this repo's tmuxinator `chezmoi` session (editor/git/shell tabs). Bind `prefix+O` → Projects and `prefix+y` → Quick Actions (already in the config).
156	
157	**Quick Actions** are chezmoi-managed alongside them, under `…/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (one TOML per action). The repo ships the four **copy-pane** actions (see [Copy focused-pane facts](#copy-focused-pane-facts-to-the-clipboard-prefixpdvs)) plus the plugin's five **starter** examples (GitHub / Google / Search Google / Open Repo / Reveal Working Dir), adapted for Linux — macOS `open` → the repo's cross-platform [`x open`](../shells/aliases.md), and the repo-select points at `daviddwlee84/*`. Because this managed dir is non-empty, herdr-plus does **not** auto-seed those examples itself (it only seeds into an *empty* dir), which is why they're vendored here; delete any TOML you don't want. Add your own by dropping a TOML here, or ship a repo-local set in `<repo>/.herdr-plus/quick-actions/`.
158	
159	> **Quick Actions are for one-off, non-interactive commands** (the shipped examples all `open <url>`). herdr-plus runs a chosen action via `sh -c` with no PTY and no interactive stdin, so an interactive TUI misbehaves — btop exits immediately, nvtop can't receive F10. For a TUI you want the lazygit-style *floating command pane* (`[[keys.command]] type="pane"`) instead — that's why **btop** (`prefix+M`) and **nvtop** (`prefix+N`) are keybinds, not Quick Actions.
160	
161	## Television integration
162	
163	Most `tv` channels (`tools`, `fleet-hosts`, `mlflow`, `kill-process`, `ssh-config`) have **non-tmux-coupled actions**, so they run unchanged in a herdr command pane — just bind a key to `tv <channel>`. Only the channels whose actions call `tmux …` need herdr-aware variants. Three ship here:
164	
165	- `herdr-sesh` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-sesh.toml`) — lists herdr sessions/workspaces + zoxide dirs; Enter dispatches `herdr session attach` / `herdr workspace focus` / `herdr workspace create --cwd` instead of `sesh connect` / `tmux switch-client`.
166	- `herdr-agent-panes` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-agent-panes.toml`) — same source as `agent-panes`, but switch/kill use `herdr pane focus` / `herdr pane close`.
167	- `herdr-review` (`dot_config/television/cable/herdr-review.toml`) — the **review-pending inbox**: lists only panes carrying the ⭐ flag (`custom_status ~ REVIEW`). Enter focuses the pane's workspace/tab and **keeps** the flag; `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read"). Bound to `prefix+i`. See the **Review-pending flag** section below.
168	
169	The original tmux-bound `sesh` / `agent-panes` channels are left intact for coexistence.
170	
171	## Agent state (replaces the 6-file workmux integration)
172	
173	herdr detects agent state natively and rolls it up into the sidebar (a blocked agent marks its pane/tab/workspace). Claude Code is detected via **screen-manifest heuristics** (terminal title + OSC progress), not lifecycle hooks. If the heuristics prove insufficient, state can be pushed explicitly:
174	
175	```bash
176	herdr pane report-agent w1:p1 --agent claude --state working
177	```
178	
179	For the trial we rely on native detection — the tmux-side workmux 🤖/💬/✅ system (Claude/OpenCode hooks → `@workmux_status`) is untouched and only applies under tmux.
180	
181	### Optional agent integrations (the onboarding "install" button)
182	
183	herdr's first-run onboarding offers to **install optional agent integrations** (`herdr integration install <agent>`), so agents report state directly instead of relying on screen heuristics. Pressing *install* sets these up for every detected agent. What it writes (verified on this machine):
184	
185	| Agent | What `herdr integration install` creates | Touches a repo-managed file? |
186	|---|---|---|
187	| claude | `~/.claude/hooks/herdr-agent-state.sh` **+ a hook entry in `~/.claude/settings.json`** | Yes — but the repo's hook-aware `modify_settings.json` merger **preserves** it (same as it does for CodeIsland). `chezmoi apply` is a no-op; it won't strip the herdr hook. |
188	| codex | `~/.codex/herdr-agent-state.sh` only | No — `~/.codex/config.toml` is untouched (identical to the chezmoi-computed target). |
189	| opencode | `~/.config/opencode/plugins/herdr-agent-state.js` (separate plugin) | No — only `workmux-status.ts` is managed; herdr's plugin coexists. |
190	| cursor | `~/.cursor/herdr-agent-state.sh` + hook | Script lives outside chezmoi; coexists. |
191	
192	These integration files are **not** vendored into the repo, so they do **not** reproduce on other machines (press *install* again there, or skip onboarding). They use herdr's own socket and do not interfere with tmux/workmux (different mechanism). To remove: `herdr integration uninstall <agent>` — and for **claude**, rerun `chezmoi apply` afterwards so the merger drops the now-removed hook from `settings.json`.
193	
194	### Config management (why `modify_`)
195	
196	herdr can rewrite `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` at runtime — finishing onboarding prepends `onboarding = false`, and the in-app *settings* popups (theme / sound / toasts / pane labels) persist there on *apply*. It edits in place and keeps existing comments, but it owns the file at runtime.
197	
198	This file was originally seeded once with the `create_` prefix so `chezmoi apply` wouldn't clobber that writeback. The cost: **repo edits never reached an already-seeded machine** — split-key rebinds and comment fixes made in the source silently never arrived without a manual `cp … source-path` refresh. That is the real reason a host could feel "out of sync" while `chezmoi diff` showed clean (the diff was clean *because* `create_` never re-touches the file). Note this is independent of hosts: `chezmoi diff` of the source against each host's live file can be byte-identical yet a repo edit still won't land until you refresh.
199	
200	It is now a **`modify_` overlay** — `dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, a small script that:
201	
202	- uses the managed body in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` as the base (comments + tmux-parity rationale), enforcing the `[theme]` / `[ui]` / `[terminal]` / `[keys]` tables on every apply, and
203	- **pulls through every other top-level key** the live file has (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`, …) so herdr's runtime writeback survives.
204	
205	TOML has no `jq`, so the merge runs in Python via `uv run --with tomlkit` (tomlkit round-trips comments **and** the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables; stdlib `tomllib` is read-only and the codex `modify_` emitter can't emit AoT). It degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw managed template, so a fresh host without Python still gets a full config. Second TOML-overlay precedent alongside `~/.codex/config.toml` (`dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`).
206	
207	To change herdr's managed config, edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` and `chezmoi apply` — it now reaches every host. Validate with `herdr server reload-config` (reports keybind collisions in its `diagnostics`; an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means the config — including array key bindings — parsed clean).
208	
209	## Persistence & restore (accidental close)
210	
211	Two native layers, no plugin needed:
212	
213	- **Client/terminal close ≠ session loss.** herdr runs a persistent **server** (named session `default`, socket `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`). Closing the terminal window just detaches — workspaces/tabs/panes and their running processes stay alive. Reattach with bare `herdr` (or `herdr session attach default`); `herdr session list` shows it `running`. This is tmux detach/reattach, built in.
214	- **Full server restart / reboot / crash.** `[session]` in the config exposes `resume_agents_on_restore = true` — resumes supported AI-agent panes back into their *native conversation sessions* after a server restart (requires the official `herdr integration install <agent>` hooks) — plus an option to save recent pane screen history across restarts. This covers the tmux-resurrect/continuum case natively, gated on those keys + integrations.
215	
216	## Remote sessions (`herdr --remote`)
217	
218	herdr can run a **local thin client attached to a herdr server on another host over SSH**:
219	
220	```bash
221	herdr --remote <ssh-target> [--session NAME] [--handoff]
222	herdr --remote local_ubuntu          # <ssh-target> is any host/alias from ~/.ssh/config
223	```
224	
225	What it does (from <https://herdr.dev/docs/remote>):
226	
227	- SSHes to `<ssh-target>`, detects the remote platform, and **auto-installs a matching herdr server binary there** — the remote does **not** need herdr pre-installed (it does need SSH access + permission to install/run a binary).
228	- Bridges your **local clipboard** (including image paste) to the remote server and keeps your **local keybindings** (`--remote-keybindings server` to use the server's instead).
229	- `--session NAME` picks/creates a named session on the remote; `--handoff` opts into live handoff.
230	
231	**Config** — the `[remote]` block in `config.toml`:
232	
233	- `manage_ssh_config = true` (default) — herdr runs the bridge SSH through a generated config that includes your `~/.ssh/config` first and adds `ServerAliveInterval`/`ServerAliveCountMax` so idle NAT/network timeouts don't drop the session. Set `false` to run plain SSH against your config unchanged.
234	- `remote_image_paste` (`[keys]`) — raw-key image-paste binding, active only under `--remote`.
235	
236	**Troubleshooting `remote platform detection failed: Connection closed by <host> port 22`**: this is a **transient SSH-level close**, not a herdr config problem. Verify the SSH path herdr uses actually works, then just retry:
237	
238	```bash
239	ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 <ssh-target> 'uname -sm'   # should print e.g. "Linux x86_64"
240	```
241	
242	If plain SSH works, retry `herdr --remote <ssh-target>`; if it keeps failing, check `~/.config/herdr/herdr-client.log` / `herdr.log` right after the failure. Common real causes: SSH auth needing an interactive prompt the bridge can't answer, or sshd rate-limiting rapid connections (`MaxStartups`).
243	
244	## Running herdr nested inside tmux (multi-remote)
245	
246	The repo's default stance is herdr **or** tmux, not nested. But you can deliberately nest — tmux as the outer window manager with several inner herdr clients, some local and some `herdr --remote <host>` to different servers. The catch is the **prefix collision**: both default to `Ctrl+b`, so outer tmux swallows it and inner herdr never sees its prefix ([herdr #759](https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr/discussions/759)).
247	
248	Three ways to resolve it, in order of preference here:
249	
250	1. **Double-prefix passthrough (recommended, zero config).** tmux keeps its default `bind -T prefix C-b send-prefix` (confirmed present in this repo — not overridden), so **`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b`** forwards a literal `Ctrl+b` to the inner herdr; its prefix bindings then work normally (`Ctrl+b Ctrl+b c` = inner new tab). No herdr or tmux change needed — classic tmux-in-tmux muscle memory.
251	2. **Rebind the inner herdr prefix.** Set `keys.prefix` (e.g. `"ctrl+a"` / `"ctrl+space"`) so the inner herdr uses a non-colliding prefix — one keystroke instead of the double-tap. Cost: it changes herdr's prefix even when run standalone (no longer matching tmux's `Ctrl+b`).
252	3. **Don't nest — use herdr's native remoting.** `herdr --remote <target> [--remote-keybindings local|server]` runs a local thin client against a remote herdr server without tmux in the middle, and herdr hosts multiple named sessions itself. For a pure "multiple remotes" need this is often cleaner than nesting; `--remote-keybindings local` (default) keeps your local keymap, `server` uses the remote's.
253	
254	Notes: this repo's tmux uses many root-table `bind -n C-*` bindings that **shadow** inner-app `Ctrl` keys, so herdr's prefix-free *direct* terminal shortcuts aren't reliable under tmux — reach herdr actions through its prefix (via 1 or 2). herdr's own `allow_nested` (config, default `false`) governs herdr-inside-**herdr** only (detected via `HERDR_ENV`), not herdr-inside-tmux.
255	
256	## Review-pending flag (mark-unread / ⭐)
257	
258	The tmux setup has a per-window bookmark (`@bookmark_status` + `toggle-bookmark.sh`, rendered via `#{?@bookmark_status,…}`). herdr has **no `#{@option}` status-bar interpolation**, so that exact mechanism doesn't port — but the *use case* that actually matters here does: **"the agent finished (`done`) but I haven't reviewed it yet."** herdr collapses a `done` pane to `idle` the moment you peek in, losing the only signal that it still needs attention.
259	
260	The fix uses herdr's **per-pane custom-status metadata**, which is orthogonal to native agent detection:
261	
262	```bash
263	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --custom-status "⭐ REVIEW"   # set (persistent — no --ttl-ms)
264	herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source review --clear-custom-status         # clear
265	```
266	
267	Verified: a pane can carry `custom_status:"⭐ REVIEW"` while `agent_status:"idle"` — so peeking in does **not** wipe the flag (the whole point). `herdr pane get` surfaces the `custom_status` field and `herdr pane list` (native JSON — **no** `--json` flag) lets the inbox enumerate flagged panes, so there is **no sidecar file**; herdr itself is the source of truth.
268	
269	Surfaces (all sharing one script, `~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh` = `dot_config/herdr/executable_review-mark.sh` — the analog of tmux's `toggle-bookmark.sh`):
270	
271	| Surface | Action |
272	|---|---|
273	| `hmark` / `hunmark` (aliases in `dot_config/shell/24_herdr.sh`) | set / clear on the current pane (ambient `$HERDR_PANE_ID`), or pass a pane id |
274	| `prefix+m` | toggle the flag on the focused pane (uses `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`) |
275	| `tv herdr-review` / `prefix+i` | the **inbox**: lists only flagged panes. `Enter` focuses & **keeps** the ⭐ (you may still be mid-review); `Alt+C` focuses **and** clears it ("mark read") |
276	
277	**Caveat — `custom_status` is a single value per pane.** The deferred usage-status driver (below) also pushes `--custom-status`; although it uses a different `--source`, `herdr pane get` exposes one flattened `custom_status`, so the two would contend for the visible label. No live conflict today (the usage driver isn't built and review flags are short-lived), but see [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
278	
279	## Copy focused-pane facts to the clipboard (`prefix+P/D/V/S`)
280	
281	Four one-keypress "grab this pane onto the clipboard" ops, all driven by one helper (`~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` = [`dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh)). It distills a herdr CLI call into human-readable text and pipes it to the repo's own [`x copy`](../shells/aliases.md) (auto-selects pbcopy / wl-copy / xclip / xsel / OSC 52; `x` is resolved by absolute-path fallback since a command-pane may run without the interactive PATH). The pane defaults to the **current focused pane** (`herdr pane current`); the keybinds pass `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, the Quick Actions pass `$HERDR_PLUS_PANE_ID`, and either falls through to the current-pane lookup when empty.
282	
283	| Op | Key | Quick Action | What lands on the clipboard |
284	|---|---|---|---|
285	| `process` | `prefix+P` | *Copy pane: process info* | foreground processes — `cmdline` + `pid` + `cwd` (from `herdr pane process-info`) |
286	| `coord` | `prefix+D` | *Copy pane: coordinate* | a paste-ready `session` / `workspace` / `tab` / `pane` id block + the `socket` path + a `# herdr pane get <pane>` line |
287	| `content` (visible) | `prefix+V` | *Copy pane: content (visible)* | the pane's on-screen text (`herdr pane read --source visible`) |
288	| `content` (scrollback) | `prefix+S` | *Copy pane: content (scrollback)* | the pane's full retained scrollback (`--source recent`) |
289	
290	The **coordinate** answers "which `session > space > tab > pane` is this?" in a form you can feed back to the CLI. herdr has **no `--session` flag** on the `pane`/`tab`/`workspace` subcommands — a session is targeted only via `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` — so the block includes the `socket=` line as the session selector (the session *name* is resolved by matching that socket against `herdr session list --json`).
291	
292	Both surfaces share the same helper: the `[[keys.command]]` binds in [`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml) and the four `copy-pane-*.toml` **Quick Actions** under `dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` (fuzzy-launched via `prefix+y`). `P/D/V/S` are uppercase (`prefix+shift+<letter>`) chosen to dodge herdr's reserved `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane) and this repo's `shift+B` (new_worktree) / `shift+R` (reload) — confirm no collision with `herdr server reload-config` (empty `diagnostics`).
293	
294	## AI usage / quota status
295	
296	herdr has **no native usage/quota/token display** (the sidebar shows agent *state* only). It does expose a per-pane hook — `herdr pane report-metadata <pane> --source ID --custom-status "…" --ttl-ms N` — that a driver could push a `"Claude 62% • Codex 78%"` label into (the same hook the **Review-pending flag** section above uses — note both write the single per-pane `custom_status`). A Codex-only community plugin ([jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit](https://github.com/jerryfane/herdr-codex-usage-kit)) already does this from the same `~/.codex` data [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) reads; nothing covers Claude/ChatGPT quota. Deferred — CodexBar's menu bar stays the multi-provider view. Design + options captured in [`backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/dotfiles/blob/main/backlog/herdr-usage-status-driver.md).
297	
298	## Gaps (no clean herdr equivalent)
299	
300	- **Seamless `Ctrl-hjkl` nvim↔pane navigation.** `vim-tmux-navigator` is tmux-coupled (the `is_vim` `ps`/`pane_tty` heuristic + the nvim plugin). herdr has no smart-splits equivalent — its pane focus is `prefix+h/j/k/l`, which won't pass through to nvim splits at the edge. Workaround: inside nvim use its own `<C-w>hjkl`. This is the biggest UX regression vs tmux.
301	- **OSC133 copy-mode** (`cpout` / `cpblock`, prompt-jump, last-output yank) is tmux-specific. herdr's copy mode (`prefix+[`) is vi-style but has no OSC133 prompt-boundary awareness. `cpcmd` (zsh history, multiplexer-agnostic) still works.
302	- **Decorative status-bar glyphs** (📌/🔖 as free-floating window labels): herdr has no `#{@option}` format-string interpolation, so tmux-style status-bar bookmarks don't port. *(The specific "mark-unread / review-pending ⭐" use case IS solved — see the **Review-pending flag** section above — via per-pane `custom_status` metadata; only the purely decorative status-bar glyph remains a gap.)*
303	- **Per-key pane resize.** tmux binds `prefix+H/J/K/L` (and `M-hjkl` for fine steps) to resize directly; herdr has no per-key resize — it uses a modal `resize_mode` (`prefix+r`), then `h/j/k/l`. Not exact parity, but a close analog.
304	
305	> **Not a gap:** vi copy-mode itself *is* native (`prefix+[`), and per-pane agent state is detected natively — the two things I expected to be missing turned out to be built in.
306

310	- [Tool managers — where tools come from](../this_repo/tool-managers.md)
311

_**Agent - sidechain (claude-opus-4-8 2026-07-17 07:33:11Z)**_

I have a complete picture. Here is my full report on the tmux URL-opening feature.

## Summary

`prefix + u` opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the current pane; selecting one opens it in the browser. It is powered by the third-party TPM plugin **`joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`** (a fork of `wenxuangm/tmux-fzf-url`). There is **no custom script** in this repo for it — the config is a single `@plugin` line using all plugin defaults. A separate, complementary feature (`tmux-open`, copy-mode `o`) also opens URLs.

Note the capital/lowercase split: `prefix + u` (lowercase) is the URL picker; `prefix + U` (uppercase) is an unrelated "CLI tools" picker via `tv tools`.

## 1. The keybinding

The binding is **not** written explicitly in this repo's config — it is registered by the plugin itself, which defaults to `u`. This repo does not override `@fzf-url-bind`, so the effective binding is `prefix + u`.

- Plugin declaration: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`
  ```
  # URL picker: prefix + u opens fzf popup with all URLs in the pane
  set -g @plugin 'joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url'
  ```
- The actual `bind-key` is created at runtime by the plugin's loader, `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.tmux` (last line):
  ```
  key="$(tmux_get '@fzf-url-bind' 'u')"
  ...
  tmux bind-key "$key" run -b "$SCRIPT_DIR/fzf-url.sh '$extra_filter' $history_limit";
  ```
  Since `@fzf-url-bind` is unset in this repo, `key` = `u`.

I confirmed there is no `bind-key u` (lowercase) and no `@fzf-url-*` override anywhere in `dot_config/tmux/`. The only `u`-family binding in `keybindings.conf.tmpl` is the uppercase `U` at line 434 (`tv tools`, a different feature).

## 2. Mechanism & installation

- **Type:** third-party tmux plugin, `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (GitHub repo `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url`; original author Wenxuan `wenxuangm`, per the header in `fzf-url.tmux`).
- **Install path:** TPM (Tmux Plugin Manager).
  - TPM itself is cloned by chezmoi external: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoiexternal.toml.tmpl:129` → clones `https://github.com/tmux-plugins/tpm.git` into `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm`.
  - TPM is run at the end of the tmux config: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/tmux/tmux.conf:26` → `run 'PATH="/opt/homebrew/opt/coreutils/libexec/gnubin:$PATH" ~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/tpm'` (macOS prepends GNU coreutils for plugins expecting GNU utils).
  - Plugins are populated on first setup by Ansible: `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4178-4200` ("Install tmux plugins via TPM", runs `~/.tmux/plugins/tpm/bin/install_plugins`, guarded by a `~/.tmux/plugins/.ansible-installed` sentinel). Manual fallback is `prefix + I` inside tmux.
  - Installed on this host at `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/` (cloned 21 Apr).

## 3. How URLs are extracted and opened (the picker)

The worker script is `/Users/david/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh`. Because this repo sets no options, it runs with defaults: `history_limit='screen'` and no extra filter.

Flow:
1. **Capture pane content** — default `limit=screen` → `content="$(tmux capture-pane -J -p)"` (visible screen only; a numeric `@fzf-url-history-limit` would instead capture `-S -<N>` lines of scrollback).
2. **Extract candidates** via multiple `grep -oE` passes over the captured text:
   - `urls`: `(https?|ftp|file):/?//...`
   - `wwws`: bare `www.` hosts, prefixed with `http://`
   - `ips`: `d.d.d.d(:port)(/path)`, prefixed with `http://`
   - `gits`: `git@...` SSH remotes rewritten to `https://`
   - `gh`: quoted `owner/repo` strings rewritten to `https://github.com/...`
   - `npm`: `import "pkg"` statements rewritten to `https://npmjs.com/package/...`
   - `extras`: only if `@fzf-url-extra-filter` is set (it is not here)
3. **Dedupe & number**: `printf ... | grep -v '^$' | sort -u | nl -w3 -s '  '`. If empty → `tmux display 'tmux-fzf-url: no URLs found'` and exit.
4. **Pick**: `fzf_filter` runs `fzf-tmux -d 35% -m -0 --no-preview --no-border` (default `@fzf-url-fzf-options`). `-m` = multi-select, `-0` = exit if no matches.
5. **Open**: the awk-extracted URL(s) are passed to `open_url`, with a log at `/tmp/tmux-$(id -u)-fzf-url.log`.

The exact opener:
```
open_url() {
    if hash xdg-open &>/dev/null; then
        nohup xdg-open "$@"
    elif hash open &>/dev/null; then
        nohup open "$@"
    elif [[ -n $BROWSER ]]; then
        nohup "$BROWSER" "$@"
    fi
}
```

## 4. Related scripts

No repo-managed script implements this — the extraction/opening lives entirely in the vendored plugin (`~/.tmux/plugins/tmux-fzf-url/fzf-url.sh` and `fzf-url.tmux`), installed via TPM as above. The many scripts under `dot_config/tmux/` (menus, sesh pickers, etc.) are unrelated.

## 5. Cross-platform open handling

Handled inside the plugin's `open_url` (above): it prefers **`xdg-open`** (Linux) if present, else **`open`** (macOS), else falls back to **`$BROWSER`**. On macOS `xdg-open` is normally absent, so `open` is used. Note the order means that if `xdg-open` exists (e.g. installed on macOS via coreutils/ports), it would win over `open`. Each launch is wrapped in `nohup` so it detaches from tmux.

## 6. Documentation

# herdr — full findings

## 1. What herdr is + how it's installed

**herdr is a Rust terminal multiplexer with built-in AI coding-agent awareness** (tracks per-pane agent state: idle / working / blocked / done). Same niche as tmux/zellij, but mouse-first and agent-native. In this repo it's a **trial tool that coexists with tmux** (you run one or the other, never nested by default).

- **Upstream repo:** `https://github.com/ogulcancelik/herdr` (confirmed by the GitHub API URL in the ansible install task, `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml:4673`: `https://api.github.com/repos/ogulcancelik/herdr/releases/latest`).
- **Docs site:** `https://herdr.dev/docs/` — config schema at `https://herdr.dev/docs/configuration/`.
- **Plugin ecosystem:** `cloudmanic/herdr-plus` (`https://github.com/cloudmanic/herdr-plus`) adds "Projects" + "Quick Actions".
- **Hierarchy:** Session → Workspace → Tab → Pane (one level deeper than tmux).

**Install** (`dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml`):
- macOS: Homebrew formula `herdr` (homebrew-core), listed in the brew block at line 89.
- Linux/Debian: GitHub release single static binary `herdr-linux-{x86_64,aarch64}` → `~/.local/bin/herdr` (install block starts at line 4628; the `--- herdr ---` comment). No tarball/unarchive.
- herdr-plus plugin: `herdr plugin install cloudmanic/herdr-plus --yes` (block at line 4713).

## 2. Config file — exact source paths

The live target is `~/.config/herdr/config.toml`, produced by a chezmoi **`modify_` overlay** (tomlkit). Two source files:

| Role | Source path |
|---|---|
| Overlay script (the `modify_`) | `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` |
| Managed body (the actual config content) | `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` |

**Helper scripts** in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/`:
- `executable_pane-copy.sh` → `~/.config/herdr/pane-copy.sh` (reads pane content/coords, pipes to clipboard)
- `executable_review-mark.sh` → review-pending ⭐ flag toggler
- `executable_new-tab-at-space-root.sh` → new tab at workspace root

**herdr-plus Quick Actions** (one TOML per action) in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/herdr/plugins/config/cloudmanic.herdr-plus/quick-actions/` — includes URL-opening starters: `github.toml`, `google.toml`, `google-search.toml`, `open-repo.toml`, `open-working-dir.toml`, plus four `copy-pane-*.toml`.

**Television channels** (herdr-aware pickers) in `/Users/david/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_config/television/cable/`: `herdr-sesh.toml`, `herdr-agent-panes.toml`, `herdr-review.toml`.

## 3. Config schema / tables

The managed body (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`) defines these tables. The overlay **enforces** `[theme]`, `[ui]`, `[terminal]`, `[keys]` on every apply and **preserves** everything herdr writes back at runtime (`onboarding`, `[session]`, `[remote]`, `[update]`, `[experimental]`).

- `[theme]` — `name`, `auto_switch`, `light_name`, `dark_name`
- `[ui]` — `mouse_capture`, `pane_borders`, `pane_gaps`, `confirm_close`, `show_agent_labels_on_pane_borders`
- `[terminal]` — `shell_mode`, `new_cwd`
- `[keys]` — **rebinds of built-in actions** + repeated **`[[keys.command]]`** array-of-tables for custom bindings
- `[session]` — `resume_agents_on_restore` (runtime-owned)
- `[remote]` — `manage_ssh_config` (runtime-owned)

Prefix is `ctrl+b` (herdr default = tmux default). **Yes, herdr has full keybinding support**, two flavors: rebinding fixed built-in actions, and defining custom command bindings that run arbitrary shell (`type = "pane"`, plus `plugin_action`). It has a first-class notion of **panes and captured pane output** (`herdr pane read`), and opening things (via custom commands → `x open`).

## 4. herdr keybinding format — this is what matters for the URL picker

### Built-in action rebinds (fixed action set, value is a key or array of keys)
```toml
[keys]
split_vertical = ["prefix+|", "prefix+%"]
reload_config = "prefix+shift+r"
switch_workspace = "prefix+ctrl+1..9"   # "N..M" indexed-range form
navigate_workspace_down = ["j", "down"]
```

### Custom command panes — `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables (the URL-picker vehicle)
This is herdr's analog of `tmux display-popup -E`. `type = "pane"` opens a temporary pane that closes when the command exits. The command runs from the focused pane's cwd and receives env vars `$HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID`, `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_CWD`.

Exact shape (verbatim examples from the current config):
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+G"
type = "pane"
command = "lazygit"
description = "lazygit (popup pane)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+U"
type = "pane"
command = "tv tools"
description = "CLI tools launcher (tv tools)"

[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+m"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/review-mark.sh toggle \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "toggle review-pending flag (⭐) on the current pane"
```

`plugin_action` type (herdr-plus):
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+y"
type = "plugin_action"
command = "cloudmanic.herdr-plus.quick-actions"
description = "herdr-plus: Quick Actions"
```

### Quick Action TOML format (herdr-plus, one file per action)
Types: `command`, `form`, `select`. Templating: `{{.Value}}`, `{{.WorkDir}}`, filters like `{{.Value | urlquery}}`.
```toml
name = "Search Google"
type = "form"
command = "x open 'https://www.google.com/search?q={{.Value | urlquery}}'"
[form]
prompt = "Search Google for"
placeholder = "e.g. herdr terminal multiplexer"
```

### Key-syntax gotchas (documented in the config comments)
- Uppercase letter = `prefix+shift+<letter>`. herdr reserves `shift+H/J/K/L` (swap-pane), `shift+g`, `shift+t`.
- `prefix+shift+<digit>` does NOT work under the Kitty keyboard protocol (shift+1 emits `!`). Use `ctrl+digit` / `alt+digit` for indexed jumps.
- Validate any edit with `herdr server reload-config` — an empty `diagnostics` array + `"status":"applied"` means no keybind collisions.

## 5. modify_ overlay mechanism (`docs/tools/herdr.md` "Config management" + CLAUDE.md line 183)

`dot_config/herdr/modify_config.toml.tmpl` is a POSIX-sh script. chezmoi pipes the live target into stdin; the script prints the new file to stdout. Merge model:
- Base = the managed template `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml` (pulled in via `{{ template "herdr/config.toml" . }}` written to a temp file through a heredoc redirect — done that way because the config contains a lone backtick in `key = "prefix+\`"` that breaks `$(...)` capture).
- For every top-level key in the live file NOT in `{theme, ui, terminal, keys}`, copy it into the base (preserves onboarding/session/remote/update/experimental writeback).
- Managed tables win wholesale (in-app theme/label overrides are re-asserted).
- Runs in Python via `uv run --no-project --with tomlkit --python '>=3.11'` (tomlkit round-trips comments + the `[[keys.command]]` array-of-tables). Degrades to system `python3`, then to emitting the raw template. Read side uses stdlib `tomllib`/`tomli`.
- **To manage a new key you edit `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`** (NOT the modify_ script). CLAUDE.md warns: never `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target.

Note: `docs/tools/agent-overlays.md` does not exist; the relevant docs are `docs/tools/herdr.md` and `docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md` (CLAUDE.md line 183 summarizes the `modify_` prefix behavior).

## 6. Directly relevant to "quickly open URLs like tmux's picker"

### The tmux model the user is copying
`dot_config/tmux/common.conf.tmpl:36-37`: `prefix + u` → plugin `joshmedeski/tmux-fzf-url` (TPM-installed) opens an fzf popup listing every URL in the pane; selecting one opens it. Also `tmux-plugins/tmux-open` (`o` in copy-mode opens highlighted URL). Documented in `dot_config/tmux/cheatsheet.md:29`.

### There is currently NO herdr URL picker
Grepping the herdr config, helpers, and tv channels found zero URL-picker binding. `prefix+u` (lowercase) is **free** in herdr — the config only binds `prefix+U` (shift+u) to `tv tools` (`.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml:130-134`). So lowercase `prefix+u` is available and matches tmux muscle memory.

### The building blocks to implement it (all already present in the repo)
1. **Extract pane text** (the URL source): `herdr pane read <pane> --source visible|recent --format text` — used in `dot_config/herdr/executable_pane-copy.sh:132`. `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` gives the focused pane inside a `[[keys.command]]`; fall back to `herdr pane current | jq -r '.result.pane.pane_id'` (pattern at pane-copy.sh:76-78).
2. **Pick a URL**: pipe extracted URLs through `fzf` (available) or a `tv` channel — same command-pane popup mechanism already used for `tv tools`/`lazygit`.
3. **Open cross-platform**: `x open <url>` — the repo's own opener (wslview / open / xdg-open), already used by every URL Quick Action (`github.toml`, `google.toml`, etc.).

### The natural implementation shape (a `[[keys.command]]` in `.chezmoitemplates/herdr/config.toml`)
```toml
[[keys.command]]
key = "prefix+u"
type = "pane"
command = "~/.config/herdr/url-pick.sh \"$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID\""
description = "URL picker — open a URL from the pane (fzf)"
```
where a new `dot_config/herdr/executable_url-pick.sh` would `herdr pane read` → grep URLs → `fzf` → `x open`. This mirrors the existing `pane-copy.sh` helper exactly (same `$HERDR_ACTIVE_PANE_ID` handling, same `herdr pane read` call, same `x` absolute-path fallback for command panes that run via `sh -c` without the interactive PATH). Alternatively it can be added purely as a herdr-plus Quick Action TOML, but the keybinding-pane route matches the tmux `prefix+u` UX one-to-one.

This exact task ("port tmux `prefix + u` URL opening to herdr") was already started in today's session `.specstory/history/2026-07-17_07-30-59Z-tmux-prefix-u-url.md` — worth reading for any prior decisions, though no URL picker has been committed to the config yet.

47	    X_BIN="$HOME/.dotfiles/bin/x"

49	    echo "pane-copy: clipboard tool 'x' not found" >&2
50	    exit 1
51	fi
